env.world:
A four-wave two-cohort absorbing latent-type Markov world, presented as ONE full-data finite probability law. The observed state space is \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A\dot\cup\{e\}\) with \(|\mathcal A|=m\ge2\), and the allowed transition graph is \(\mathcal G=(\mathcal A\times\mathcal S)\cup\{(e,e)\}\), so the exit state \(e\) is absorbing. The world object is a probability law \(P\) on the finite set of full-data atoms
\[
 a=\bigl(D,\;Z,\;(X_t(0))_{t\le3},\;(X_t(1))_{t\le3},\;(X_t)_{t\le3}\bigr)
 \in\{0,1\}\times\{1,\ldots,J\}\times\mathcal S^4\times\mathcal S^4\times\mathcal S^4,
\]
with \(D=1\) denoting adoption at date \(3\), \(Z\) the time-invariant latent type with fixed known \(2\le J\le m\), \(X_t(r)\) the potential state at date \(t\) under treatment path \(r\), and \(X_t\) the recorded state; the observed panel is \(O=(D,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\). Every other object of the world is a marginal, conditional, or ratio of that single law rather than separate data: the cohort masses \(P(D=d)\), the type masses \(\pi_j^d\), the observed cell-probability vector \(p\) on the \(N_m=2\sum_{r=0}^4m^r\) absorption-legal four-wave cells, the at-risk masses \(\alpha_j^d\) and unnormalized component sublaws \(s_j^d\), the contributions \(\nu_j\), the at-risk effects \(\eta_j\), the conditional effects \(\tau_j\), the aggregate \(\tau\), the stacked target \(\theta_J=(\nu_1^\top,\ldots,\nu_J^\top,\tau^\top)^\top\), the observed slices \(A_{xy}^d\) and predecessor masses \(m_x^d\), the selected minors \(M_{xy}^d\), the cycle-product operator \(K^d\), and the latent factors \(B_x^{d,\mathcal A}\), \(D_{xy}\), \(C_y^d\). The transition kernels are not primitive data either: \(H_j^d\), \(Q_j\), \(U_j\), \(V_j\) are row-stochastic matrices supported on \(\mathcal G\) against which a law may factorize — conditional on \((D,Z)\), the untreated path law is the product \((H_j^d,Q_j,U_j)\) and the treated path law is \((H_j^d,Q_j,V_j)\), the two continuations sharing the date-\(2\) coordinate — and the factual first-post kernel is \(R_j^d=U_j\) for \(d=0\), \(R_j^d=V_j\) for \(d=1\). Consistency \(X_t=X_t(D)\), no anticipation \(X_t(1)=X_t(0)\) for \(t\le2\), and absorption are restrictions on the support of the same law. Fixed ex ante selections \(\mathcal U,\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal A\) with \(|\mathcal U|=|\mathcal V|=J\) and anchors \(x_0\neq x_1\), \(y_0\neq y_1\) in \(\mathcal A\) index the slices and minors.
